topic: Publication date of Mead and Conway's 'Introduction to VLSI Systems'
disagreement: The Computer History Museum's Silicon Engine page dates the book to 1979 (Addison-Wesley, December 1979) while the National Research Council history and CHM's own object record give 1980; Conway's quoted Hall of Fame entry says 1978.
possible_reasons: definition: December 1979 printing vs 1980 copyright/imprint date
rationale: Both are defensible: the book appears to have been printed in December 1979 with a 1980 copyright date; the 1978 date refers to prepublication drafts.
remaining_uncertainty: Title-page copyright date not inspected directly in this run.

topic: Fabless share of IC sales in 2019
disagreement: IC Insights (April 2021) gives 29.9%; TechInsights (June 2025), its successor, gives 30.5%.
possible_reasons: data vintage: later revision of company sales
population: 'fabless/system IC companies' vs 'fabless IC' labels
rationale: Later vintage from the same research lineage, presumably incorporating revisions.
remaining_uncertainty: The revision is not explained in either public summary; the methodology for classifying system companies (e.g. HiSilicon, Apple) is not disclosed.

topic: Fabless share of the market in 2002
disagreement: EDN (Feb 2003, citing IC Insights) gives 'nearly 12% of worldwide chip revenue' for 2002; IC Insights' 2021 bulletin gives 13% of the total IC market.
possible_reasons: denominator: total semiconductor ('chip') revenue including discretes/opto vs IC-only market
data vintage: preliminary early-2003 estimate vs later revised series
rationale: Use the IC-only series for a consistent time series; the EDN figure has a wider denominator and an earlier vintage.
remaining_uncertainty: Neither source publishes the underlying dollar figures for the 2002 IC market used.

topic: Which company was the first fabless chip company
disagreement: Xilinx says it was set up as a fabless company in February 1984; ChipHistory.org calls Chips and Technologies (co-founded 1985 by Gordon Campbell) the first successful fabless company and Campbell the 'father' of the fabless industry.
possible_reasons: founding date ambiguity for C&T (1984 vs 1985 in secondary sources)
both are self-interested or advocacy sources
rationale: Both statements can hold: Xilinx was incorporated earlier (Feb 1984, per its 10-K) as fabless; C&T is credited with proving the model in a large market (PC chipsets).
remaining_uncertainty: No neutral primary source (e.g. contemporary FSA or US government document) adjudicating 'first' was found.
